claim: A round-folded ASCON-128 permutation (6 rounds/cycle) on Artix-7 achieves 3535.91 Mbps throughput at 1.19 Mbps/LUT efficiency.
stance_target: FPGA lightweight-crypto Verilog/VHDL projects can achieve publishable, quantifiable throughput-to-area improvements
quoted_support: the ASCON-128 implementation in this work achieves a throughput of 3535.91 Mbps with an efficiency of 1.19 Mbps/LUT.

claim: ASCON-128a with a 4-round-per-cycle permutation on Artix-7 reaches 5333.3 Mbps throughput at 2.44 Mbps/LUT, beating the best prior design's 1683.2 Mbps / 0.887 Mbps/LUT.
stance_target: throughput-to-area optimization is a viable novelty angle for undergraduate crypto-FPGA papers
quoted_support: The ASCON-128a implementation from this work further improves upon these results, achieving the highest throughput of 5333.3 Mbps with an better efficiency of 2.44 Mbps/LUT.

claim: On Kintex-7, the proposed ASCON-128a design reaches 10158 Mbps throughput with 3.32 Mbps/LUT efficiency, the highest among compared implementations.
stance_target: novel throughput-to-area FPGA crypto architecture claim
quoted_support: The ASCON-128a implementation in this work further enhances these results, demonstrating a throughput of 10158 Mbps and an efficiency of 3.32 Mbps/LUT, which is the highest among the implementations compared.

claim: ASCON was selected as the NIST Lightweight Cryptography standard winner in February 2023, with the official standard published June 16, 2023.
stance_target: background legitimacy of ASCON as a research topic
quoted_support: After further evaluations, the ASCON family was declared the winner in February 2023, and the official NIST standard was published on June 16, 2023.

claim: The paper's Spartan-7 implementation of ASCON-128a reaches 5333.33 Mbps at 2.45 Mbps/LUT, a 98.63% throughput-to-area improvement versus best Spartan-6 design (1116.4 Mbps, 0.584 Mbps/LUT).
stance_target: older/cheaper FPGA families still show large gains from modern toolchain and round-folding design
scope_conditions: Spartan-7 vs Spartan-6 comparison; caveat that some improvement is due to platform generation not just design
quoted_support: Our ASCON-128 implementation on the Spartan-7 FPGA achieves a throughput of 3440.86 Mbps with an efficiency of 1.16 Mbps/LUT, and the ASCON-128a implementation reaches an impressive 5333.33 Mbps with an efficiency of 2.45 Mbps/LUT.
